title: Dark bands under overhangs, objects and digs: one mechanism, three costumes
question: Storing the genesis void per *cell* instead of per column kills panels 1 and 3 outright, but leaves panel 2 (the open pit) still black, because those cells really were rock. Is a dug-out pit reading as cave acceptable, or must the fix cover that too?
context_md:
Answering your note on the pond card ("a bigger issue with shadows/background"). **It is the background baseline, not a shadow.** There is no shadow caster in the engine at all — `sky::apply_light` is a global day/night multiplier with no occlusion term, and fake AO was measured and cut.

All three panels are one mechanism: `World::sky_surface` records the topmost `Solid`/`Powder` **per column**, frozen on frame 1, and everything at or below it in that column is "inside the ground" forever. Two consumers read it — `background_at` fades empty cells to `UNDERGROUND` over 24 rows (sqrt ramp, saturates at full black), and `TerrainLight::Depth` grades non-empty cells (rock, soil, **and water**) down to 0.62.

Because the test is "is there anything solid above me in this column", it cannot tell a cave roof from a cliff brow, a hillside from a rock suspended in mid-air, or rock you removed from rock that was never there.

Measured, not inferred:

- The depth grade is **not** the cause of the black. `light=flat` (F10 off) leaves the pit in panel 2 exactly as black — the empty-cell cave fade does all of it. The grade is what darkens the *water* on your pond card.
- New probe `examples/underground_probe.rs` counts open air (flood-reachable from the sky) that the renderer draws as cave. Numbers per panel below.

`Reports/dead-ends.md` §977 forbids going back to inferring this from geometry and says *"revisit only by storing more history"*. One bit per cell — "was this enclosed at genesis" — is that: a 5.8 ms flood fill once at generation, 164 KB at 2048x640, no width threshold anywhere, and it keeps every property the current rule was chosen for (a dug shaft of any width stays a tunnel, a built roof stays outdoors).
